> **This is the model comparison, measured before the judge gained its asksAboutFacts field.** It is
> what justified shipping Super with reasoning off, and that argument still holds: Lightning credited a
> rubric item on 40% of the lines that should score nothing, Super on none. The default row's own
> numbers have since been re-measured against the current prompt in judge.default.md, and a partial run
> now writes beside this file rather than over it.

## Judge accuracy (demo-cough, 50 labelled lines each)

| Judge setting | Exact lines | Precision | Recall | False unlocks | Failures | Cost | Per line (mean / 95th pct) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nano, reasoning off | 40% | 75% | 17% | 7% | 0 | $0.0026 | 0.7 s / 1.2 s |
| Lightning, reasoning off | 82% | 70% | 94% | 40% | 0 | $0.0025 | 0.4 s / 0.4 s |
| Super, reasoning off (default) | 90% | 86% | 89% | 0% | 0 | $0.0112 | 1.0 s / 1.1 s |
| Super, reasoning on | 98% | 97% | 100% | 0% | 0 | $0.0283 | 3.2 s / 4.9 s |
| Ultra, reasoning off | 96% | 95% | 100% | 0% | 0 | $0.0397 | 1.0 s / 1.1 s |

Exact lines counts a failed line as wrong. False unlocks: off-topic and injection lines that would have unlocked a fact, failed lines left out. Time per line includes any repair call. Cost is what the budget charged, failed attempts included.
